import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# The dataset is provided as a string, so we use io.StringIO to read it like a file.
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'has_video_4k' numerical (0/1) to a more descriptive categorical label for better legend readability.
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set a professional seaborn style for better aesthetics.
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot.
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Model Year and Price.
# - 'model_year' on the x-axis to show trends over time.
# - 'price_usd' on the y-axis as a key dependent variable.
# - 'brand' is mapped to 'hue' to differentiate camera brands by color.
# - 'has_video_4k_label' is mapped to 'style' to differentiate cameras with/without 4K video by marker style.
# - 's' sets the size of the markers, 'edgecolor' and 'alpha' improve visibility.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x="model_year",
    y="price_usd",
    hue="brand",
    style="has_video_4k_label",
    s=250, # Marker size
    edgecolor="black", # Black border for markers
    alpha=0.8, # Transparency of markers
    legend='full' # Display the full legend
)

# Annotate each point with additional key information (Megapixels and Sensor Type)
# This is particularly useful for small datasets to provide immediate context for each data point.
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(row['model_year'] + 0.1, row['price_usd'] + 50,
             f"{row['megapixels']}MP | {row['sensor_type']}",
             fontsize=9, ha='left', va='bottom', color='dimgray')

# Set the title and labels for the axes.
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Model Year, by Brand and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Ensure all unique model years are displayed on the x-axis for clarity.
plt.xticks(df['model_year'].unique().tolist())

# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points.
plt.legend(title='Camera Features', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Add a grid for easier reading of values.
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/titles from being cut off.
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file named 'output.png'.
plt.savefig('output.png')
